newsitem.title: USA: U.S. manufacturers' profits slipped as 1996 ended.
newsitem.headline: U.S. manufacturers' profits slipped as 1996 ended.

text.p: Profits of U.S. manufacturing companies slipped in the final quarter of last year despite rising sales, the Commerce Department said Monday.
A quarterly survey of about 8,300 companies showed that profits dipped in the fourth quarter to a seasonally adjusted 6.1 cents per dollar of sales from 6.5 cents in the third quarter of the year.

The fourth-quarter drop, which was especially sharp among makers of nondurable goods, occurred as the nation's gross domestic product, or GDP, accelerated to a vigorous 3.8 percent annual rate from 2.1 percent in the third quarter.

Manufacturers' profits after taxes during the fourth quarter were a seasonally adjusted $58.49 billion on net sales of $961.34 billion. In the third quarter, profits were a higher $61.74 billion on net sales of $948.91 billion.

The decline in fourth-quarter profits was concentrated among producers of nondurable goods, especially makers of chemicals, the department said. Rubber, paper and textile producers also reported profit declines, it said.
As a group, nondurable goods producers reported that their profits fell to $29.89 billion in the fourth quarter from $33.58 billion in the third quarter, the department said.
Producers of longer-lasting durable goods reported that their profits after taxes rose slightly to a seasonally adjusted $28.6 billion in the fourth quarter from $28.16 billion in the third quarter.
The department also reported fourth-quarter profits and sales for big retail companies with assets of $50 million or more, showing gains in both sales and profits from the third- quarter pace.
Retailers' profits after taxes averaged 2.4 cents per sales dollar in the fourth quarter, up from 2 cents in the third quarter.

The profit figures for retailers are not adjusted for seasonal variations. Total profits were $6.46 billion on sales of $270.94 billion in the fourth quarter, up from $4.83 billion on sales of $237.02 billion in the third quarter.
